newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills rally as kiwi gains vs Aussie/US dollars.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills rally as kiwi gains vs Aussie/US dollars.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.28 (PREV 92.10) 90-DAYS 8.30 (PREV 8.58)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.25 PCT (PREV 8.25) US 5-YR 6.07 (PREV 6.03)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 765.75 (PREV 760.65) Reuters NZ MCI -59 vs -64
New Zealand's key 90-day bank bill rates rallied 28 points on Thursday to close at 8.30 percent after the Kiwi dollar made solid gains against the Australian and U.S. dollars.

The Trade-Weighted Index gained 46 points from Wednesday's close to 64.86 as the Kiwi rose to A$0.8870/86 (A$0.8788/09 at Wednesday's close) and to US$0.6515/22, prompting the short end rally, dealers said.
"It's really following on from the currency and the TWI being a lot higher," said one.
"After lunchtime the Kiwi dollar got paid up over (U.S. cents) 65 figure and there was Aussie wages data out which was pretty bullish."
Australian seasonally adjusted weekly ordinary time wages rose 0.5 percent in the May quarter lending weight to the belief that rates may fall there soon.

"There was also some talk of a recommendation from Merrill Lynch to sell Aussie and buy Kiwi -- it may only have been a rumour -- and that caused a pretty significant rally in our short end," the dealer said.
"And we saw Asian buying of T-bills, from the one to three months, pretty decent volumes there."
Money market strength flowed through into the short end of the bond curve, where the 02/01 bond yield rallied nine points to 6.98 percent.
The long end, however, remained reasonably subdued.
The 11/06 bond yield opened eight points weaker on offshore selling overnight, but recovered to close around its Wednesday closing level at 6.76 percent.
Dealers said there was still an offer tone in the long end, but they expected short bonds to hold their gains for the time being with the currency seen edging higher.
"I would expect the currency to fall again at some stage, but I don't expect it to get slammed. There'll probably be a bit more of a squeeze on the upside in the short-term," a dealer said.
